subject: Follow-up: Operational controls for EU→US data transfers (DPF evidence & runbooks)
messages:
From: Jarvis Collins <jarvis.collins@medsecure.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medsecure.com
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: operational controls and runbooks for DPF evidence

Hi Monica / Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our security & legal review for the upcoming contract, MedSecure must validate operational controls supporting EU→US transfers under the Data Protection Framework (DPF). Our RFP spreadsheet (attached) highlights a number of evidence requests — we need concrete artifacts for:

- Runtime controls (KMS/HSM usage, key rotation policy, envelope encryption)
- Audit logging: field-level masking, retention windows, access review cadence
- Procedures: incident response runbook for exfiltration, cross-border data access escalation
- Sub-processor list and their contracts showing SCCs / DPA annex references

Can you confirm what you can produce within 7 business days? Also please indicate whether the evidence corresponds to your Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployment options — MedSecure will likely require Private (VPC) but needs the mapping.

Attached: MedSecure_DPF_questionnaire_v3.xlsx (we added line numbers in the left column).

Regards,
Jarvis
Jarvis Collins
Head of Security Programs
MedSecure Health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jarvis Collins <jarvis.collins@medsecure.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational controls and runbooks for DPF evidence

Hi Jarvis — thanks for the clear spreadsheet, we can do this. A few clarifying items before we prepare the bundle:

1) Scope: do you want evidence mapped to each DPF line item (row numbers) or a consolidated controls matrix that cites the supporting artifact per line? We can do both but mapping will take longer.

2) Deployment mode: you mentioned Private (VPC). Can you confirm whether MedSecure expects customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key/HSM) or is Redwood-managed KMS acceptable for the first-pass evidence? For Private deployments we support both.

3) SOC 2 /scope: does your team require SOC 2 Type II for the hosted control set, or will an internal audit checklist + system logs suffice for Dedicated/Private?

Planned deliverables (proposed):
- Controls matrix (spreadsheet) mapping DPF criteria to Redwood controls and sample artifacts
- Redacted audit log(s) sample + schema and retention policy (pseudo-sanitized)
- KMS architecture diagram + key rotation policy excerpt
- DPA Annex excerpt showing cross-border transfer terms and fallback routing
- Sub-processor CSV + contract reference list

I'll start drafting the controls matrix and will attach version 1 this afternoon. If you can reply on questions 1-3 we'll tailor the attachments.

Thanks — looping Neha (Privacy Lead) and Laura (Legal) for their input.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134
LinkedIn: /in/monica-patel

Attachment: redwood_dpf_controls_matrix_v1.xlsx

From: Jarvis Collins <jarvis.collins@medsecure.com>

Cc: procurement@medsecure.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational controls and runbooks for DPF evidence

Monica — thanks. Quick clarifications inline and answers to your Qs:

> 1) Scope: do you want evidence mapped to each DPF line item (row numbers) or a consolidated controls matrix that cites the supporting artifact per line?

We'd prefer a per-line mapping (our reviewers are strict), but a consolidated matrix that links to per-line artifacts is acceptable. If you can deliver the consolidated matrix this week and the per-line mapping next week that works.

> 2) Deployment mode: do you expect BYOK/HSM or Redwood-managed KMS?

MedSecure is open to Redwood-managed KMS for PoC, but procurement will require BYOK/HSM for production Private deployments. Please flag any gaps.

> 3) SOC 2 scope?

We require SOC 2 Type II for Hosted; for Private deployments we will still review a controls-based evidence bundle and request an executed DPA Annex that references SCCs/DPF.

Timeline: we need the consolidated matrix + artifacts by EOD next Wednesday (2026-10-13) to keep our procurement timeline. I attached a short timeline excerpt.

Thanks,
Jarvis

Attachment: MedSecure_RFP_timeline.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jarvis Collins <jarvis.collins@medsecure.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational controls and runbooks for DPF evidence

Hi Jarvis / Monica / Laura,

Thanks — below is an executive mapping and list of deliverables we will provide. I'll highlight where MedSecure's BYOK/HSM requirement for production Private deployment introduces differences in the artifacts.

--- Executive mapping (high level) ---
1) Legal basis & DPF framing:
- We will provide: DPA Annex excerpt (redacted), Transfer Impact Assessment executive summary, and clause references to SCCs/DPF equivalence statements.
- Notes: Redwood supports DPF-compatibility for EU→US transfers via our contractual DPA Annex + technical safeguards (encryption, access controls). For customers requiring BYOK/HSM we provide a deployment pattern that isolates key custodianship to the customer and documents key escrow procedures.

2) Technical measures — encryption & keys:
- Evidence: KMS architecture diagram (hosted vs private), key lifecycle policy (rotation, separation of duties), sample CMK metadata (no plaintext keys), and HSM attestation pattern for BYOK/HSM.
- For Private+BYOK: key operations are performed in customer-managed HSM; our logs show only key IDs (no key material).

3) Audit logging & retention:
- Evidence: sample redacted audit log slices (pseudo-anonymized), log schema doc, retention policy (default 365 days; configurable for Private), and example access-review cadence screenshots from the Console.
- Note: logs include per-token processing metadata (latency, model id, client id) but request/response payloads are redacted in hosted samples. For Private deployments audits can be configured to preserve full payloads under customer control.

4) Access controls & least privilege:
- Evidence: IAM role matrix, RBAC config export, SSO / SCIM integration notes, and example access-review reports.

5) Incident response & breach playbook:
- Evidence: Incident runbook excerpt for suspected exfiltration, timeline templates, and notification SLA commitments (72 hours SR for confirmed breaches + 24h initial acknowledgement).

6) Sub-processors & contracts:
- Evidence: current sub-processor roster (.csv), contract reference list pointing to SCCs/DPA annex clauses and dates of last contract updates.

7) Operational controls unique to inference:
- Evidence: KV cache management description, model snapshotting policy, purge/TTL controls for cached prefixes, and instructions for disabling caching in Dedicated/Private if required.
- Redaction note: prefix caching can be disabled per-customer in Private deployments to meet stricter PD requirements.

8) Data localization and routing:
- Evidence: routing policy docs, region mapping (data plane locations), and fallback routing policy (automatic routing to alternate region with notification).

--- Deliverables we will attach (consolidated bundle) ---
- redwood_dpf_controls_matrix_v1.xlsx (consolidated mapping to your line numbers)
- redwood_dpf_evidence_bundle.zip (contains redacted logs, KMS policy excerpt, runbook excerpts, IAM exports)
- subprocessors_v2.csv (current sub-processor list + contract dates)
- DPA_Annex_excerpt_redacted.pdf (cross-border transfer clauses referencing SCCs/DPF)

--- Notes on BYOK/HSM requirement ---
If MedSecure requires BYOK/HSM in production Private deployment we will:
- Provide architecture diagrams and an implementation checklist for customer-managed HSM (hardware, network egress, key rotation process)
- Deliver a short on-prem verification checklist and sample attestation template for HSM setup
- Confirm that evidence for BYOK will show key IDs only; Redwood cannot provide HSM key material or KMS root private keys.

We will prepare the consolidated matrix and the redacted evidence bundle by EOD 2026-10-13 as requested. If any item above requires deeper technical artifacts (for example, raw log exports or HSM attestation reports) please flag — those take additional approvals and timelines.

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Lead | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0248
